findings.evidenceJa: 『なんてね。謝るべきところは、本当はそこじゃないのもわかってます』
findings.explanation: Setsuna is not retracting the preceding apology as a joke. なんてね marks a rueful self-correction: she knows that drunkenly neglecting her guest is not what she truly owes Haruki an apology for. 'I'm just kidding' falsely makes the sincere apology itself facetious.
findings.japanese:
『なんてね。
謝るべきところは、
本当はそこじゃないのもわかってます』
findings.todokanai: "I'm just kidding. I know that if I'm truly going to apologize, I shouldn't be apologizing for this in particular."

findings.highlight: And now that I've strayed away from what I was supposed to be working toward, all I have left is to live with the fact that my heart was stolen by another woman.
findings.evidenceJa:
俺が、他の女性に心を奪われたという事実だけが残り、
肝心の『これから』を見失ってしまったから…
findings.explanation: Only the fact that Haruki's heart was taken by another woman remains while he has lost sight of the crucial future; the English makes straying from his goal the setup and does not directly state the lost future.
findings.japanese:
俺が、他の女性に心を奪われたという事実だけが残り、
肝心の『これから』を見失ってしまったから…
findings.todokanai: And now that I've strayed away from what I was supposed to be working toward, all I have left is to live with the fact that my heart was stolen by another woman.

findings.highlight: contact me at the place I'm about to tell you right now
findings.evidenceJa: 「うん、うん…それでいいと思う。で、どうしても無理だと思ったら、今から言うところに連絡しなさい」
findings.explanation: Mari tells Suzuki that if the direct approach fails, she should contact the person or office Mari is about to name. The English tells Suzuki to contact Mari herself 'at the place,' even though Mari is leaving and the next line explains that the named contact is someone who helped her as a new employee.
findings.japanese:
「うん、うん…それでいいと思う。
で、どうしても無理だと思ったら、
今から言うところに連絡しなさい」
findings.todokanai: "Mhm, mhmm… that's fine with me. Well, if it's really impossible no matter what, contact me at the place I'm about to tell you right now."

findings.highlight: it's not like I have anything left to teach her anyway
findings.evidenceJa: 「いい加減独り立ちしてもらわないと困るわよね。…もう、教えることもできなくなるんだし」
findings.explanation: Suzuki has to become independent because Mari will soon no longer be able to teach her after moving abroad. The English says Mari has nothing left to teach, changing forced separation from her protégé into completion of Suzuki's training.
findings.japanese:
「いい加減独り立ちしてもらわないと困るわよね。
…もう、教えることもできなくなるんだし」
findings.todokanai: "If she doesn't pull herself together and stand up for herself, it'll be a problem… though it's not like I have anything left to teach her anyway."

findings.highlight: "Just when I thought you were going to break into tears in public, you get a call from work and instantly recover, and then you immediately start crying after you're finished… you're all over the place."
findings.evidenceJa:
「人前でわんわん泣いてたと思ったら、
仕事の電話入った途端に復活するわ、
終わったらまたすぐ泣き出すわ…メリハリありすぎ」
findings.explanation: Sawako says Mari had been bawling in public, recovered instantly for a work call, then resumed crying afterward; the English changes the first fact into Sawako merely thinking Mari was about to cry.
findings.japanese:
「人前でわんわん泣いてたと思ったら、
仕事の電話入った途端に復活するわ、
終わったらまたすぐ泣き出すわ…メリハリありすぎ」
findings.todokanai: "Just when I thought you were going to break into tears in public, you get a call from work and instantly recover, and then you immediately start crying after you're finished… you're all over the place."

findings.highlight: You could get on your knees and plead with him the moment you see him.
findings.evidenceJa: 「相手に会いに行って土下座するとか。『あなたにはまだまだ先がある。けれど私のチャンスはもう今しかないの』って…」
findings.explanation: Sawako proposes that Mari meet the rival woman, Setsuna, kneel, and plead: 'You still have your whole future ahead of you, but this is my only chance.' The English tells Mari to plead with Haruki and then makes the one remaining chance his, reversing the addressee and the age-based argument.
findings.japanese:
「相手に会いに行って土下座するとか。
『あなたにはまだまだ先がある。
けれど私のチャンスはもう今しかないの』って…」
findings.todokanai: "You could get on your knees and plead with him the moment you see him. Tell him that he still has a long road ahead of him, but this is the one chance he has left…"

findings.highlight: do you really have to go over there?
findings.evidenceJa: 麻理、あんた向こうで本当にやっていけるの？世の中、やっぱ仕事だけじゃ生きていけないよ？」
findings.explanation: Sawako asks whether Mari will really be able to cope or make a life for herself there, given that work alone is not enough to live on. The English asks whether she really has to go, changing concern about Mari's emotional viability abroad into a challenge to the transfer's necessity.
findings.japanese:
麻理、あんた向こうで本当にやっていけるの？
世の中、やっぱ仕事だけじゃ生きていけないよ？」
findings.todokanai: Mari, do you really have to go over there? You know you can't just live on with only your work with you, right?"
